title: Introduce batch/cache heuristic compiler and unit-price prober
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Add a compiler that generates tenant-scoped batch/cache defaults and a probing tool that estimates per-unit inference cost for candidate batching+quantization profiles; safe-by-default rollouts and a dry-run CLI for operator validation.
description: Context and motivation: Customers frequently ask for reliable, automated defaults for batching and KV-cache behavior plus guidance on quantization profiles. We observed repeated ops work where on-call or SRE teams had to hand-tune tenant defaults after spikes; operators lacked a safe way to estimate per-token unit prices for combinations of batch shape, prefill strategy, and quant tier. This PR introduces two pieces: 1) a heuristic compiler that synthesizes tenant-level candidate defaults (batch_size, max_latency_target, prefill_strategy, cache_ttl, quant_tier_hint) from historical workload slices and model performance profiles; and 2) a unit-price prober that runs controlled microbenchmarks (shadow requests + synthetic prefixes) against a matrix of batch/cache/quant settings to estimate dollars-per-1k-tokens and 95th percentile latency. Both components are intended for Redwood Dedicated + Private deployments and integrate with the Console recommendations UI and the optimize CLI. Key goals: safe outputs (never auto-apply to production without explicit operator consent), reproducible probes, lightweight runtime overhead for the compiler, and clear telemetry to correlate price vs latency vs quality.

review_comments: Marco Reyes: Please make sure the compiler never overwrites tenant runtime defaults automatically. If you haven't already, gate the API behind an opt-in flag and require operator approval in the Console.

Ava Chen (author): Addressed — compiler outputs are now saved as 'candidate_defaults' and written to a staging collection; the Console endpoint exposes an 'apply' action requiring a 2-step confirmation.

merge_details: Merged by Marco Reyes on 2024-11-27 via squash and merge. Merge commit message: 'econ: add heuristic compiler + unit-price prober; CLI + Console integration; safe-by-default candidate outputs.'
notes_for_ops: Operator runbook updated (infra/runbooks/econ_probing.md). Important: always run prober in shadow mode first (-m shadow) for live tenants and use --simulate to validate compiled defaults. Prober requires econ:probe RBAC permission and may consume reserved GPU credits when running large matrices.
testing_notes: Unit and integration tests added. Prober integration tests use a mocked runtime by default; an optional CI job exercises the prober against a tiny GPU instance labeled 'perf-smoke'. Test coverage includes edge cases where historical workload is sparse and where quant tier profiles are missing.
performance_summary: In local staging runs the compiler produced candidate defaults that reduced median per-token cost by ~9% for chat workloads and enabled a 12% throughput increase for high-concurrency sequence-generation tests when combined with quant-tier 'q4_0' suggestions. Prober median estimates matched actual billing-derived unit prices within 6% on average across the sampled tenant set.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: automated suggestions could encourage aggressive quantization and degrade output quality. Mitigation: classifier-based quality checks are in place; recommendations include conservative quality gates and do not auto-apply. Risk: prober may overload small clusters; mitigation: default probe matrix is constrained and the runbook requires operator approval for large matrices.
ui_impact: Small - Console adds a recommendations panel with a preview of compiler outputs and an 'apply' button that triggers a guarded workflow. Changes are feature-flagged and off by default for existing tenants.
rollback_plan: If regressions are detected, operators can revoke applied candidate defaults via Console (history and revert button). The compiler writes every plan to a staging collection with metadata to reconstruct previous values.
follow_up_work: 1) Add a lightweight A/B evaluator to measure quality delta after applying a candidate default. 2) Expose a multi-tenant batch-suggestion API for platform teams. 3) Add autoscheduler recommendations that combine tenant budgets with demand curves.
human_readable_summary: This PR adds a safe, auditable way to generate recommended batching and cache defaults and a reproducible tool to estimate per-token cost for candidate settings. It enables operators to make informed trade-offs between latency, cost, and quality with minimal manual tuning.
changelog_entry: Added: heuristic compiler for batch/cache defaults; unit-price prober with CLI and Console integration; operator runbook and telemetry events for econ recommendations.
